title: Rise in the Full-Term Risk Premium for Building-Limit Increases on Loan Transactions — NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
## Measuring the rise in the full-term risk premium — increase of the building limit recorded for a loan transaction (NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own))

For a pending increase of the building limit recorded for a loan transaction on a tier that carries no ICC coverage, the rise in the full-term risk premium on which the charge is measured is set by the first line below that holds:

| Situation on the records | Rise in the full-term risk premium |
|---|---|
| The request carries no full-term risk premium from the rating engine | No rise |
| A re-rate credit from an applied Elevation Certificate was booked on the current term after the request was recorded | The request's full-term risk premium less the risk premium booked for the term at its start, because both figures stand on the rating basis the request was rated on |
| Otherwise | The request's full-term risk premium less the rated risk premium on the policy |

The risk premium booked for the term at its start is the risk premium charged for the current term at new business or at renewal. A re-rate credit counts here only when it is a credit on the risk premium line from an applied Elevation Certificate, posted on the current term after the date the request was recorded.

*Hypothetical illustration.* A request carries a full-term risk premium of 1,500.00 dollars; the rated risk premium on the policy is 1,300.00 dollars and the risk premium booked for the term at its start was 1,400.00 dollars. With no such re-rate credit the rise is 200.00 dollars (1,500.00 less 1,300.00). Had a re-rate credit from an applied certificate been posted on the current term after the request was recorded, the rise would be 100.00 dollars (1,500.00 less 1,400.00).
